answer.question: Are we on pace to hit goal, and where do we land by election day if nothing changes?
answer.answer:
Not quite — the program is ahead of its goal to date but on current pace projects to finish short by 3,303 doors (94.6% of goal), with Eastgate and Harbor both missing and only Northside beating its goal.

- Program to date (Sep 21 – Oct 18): 33,503 doors against a goal to date of 32,431 — 103.3% of goal to date [view:v_office_pace_total]
- Projection with nothing changing: 57,329 doors by Election Day vs a goal of 60,632, a shortfall of 3,303 doors (94.6% of goal) [view:v_office_pace_total]
- Northside: 13,647 doors, 112.5% of goal to date; projected 23,583 vs 22,675 goal, so +908 [view:v_office_pace]
- Harbor: 11,351 doors, 105.3% of goal to date; projected 19,150 vs 20,157 goal, so −1,007 [view:v_office_pace]
- Eastgate: 8,505 doors, 89.3% of goal to date; projected 14,596 vs 17,800 goal, so −3,204 [view:v_office_pace]
- To close the gap the program needs 33.3 shifts per day over the 16 knocking days left (Oct 19 – Nov 3) against 29.3 per day last week — 4.1 extra shifts per day; Eastgate alone needs 4.4 more [view:v_office_pace_total] [view:v_office_pace]

How it's worked out: the projection is doors to date plus the last 7 days' average daily doors times the 16 knocking days left; a negative projected-vs-goal figure is the shortfall [doc:program-plan#pace-and-projection].

answer.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?
answer.answer:
**Ask for more doors first.** At the current pace you'd run out of first-pass turf before Election Day, so the program plan says to request new turf rather than start second passes.

- Remaining capacity: 1,489.1 average daily doors last 7 days × 16 knocking days left = about 23,826 doors of capacity, against only 10,393 untouched doors left in the turf [view:v_office_pace_total].
- The rule: when capacity for the rest of the program is larger than the untouched doors left, ask the client for more doors first, because new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate; a second pass on not-home doors contacts at roughly half that rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass].
- You are also behind overall: projected 57,329 doors vs a 60,632 goal, a shortfall of 3,303 (94.6% of goal), which would need 4.1 extra shifts per day [view:v_office_pace_total].
- By office, the turf squeeze is uneven: Harbor has 8,096 untouched doors vs 487.4/day × 16 ≈ 7,798 of capacity, while Northside (1,114 untouched) and Eastgate (1,183 untouched) have far more capacity than turf [view:v_office_pace].
- Eastgate is both the weakest office (89.3% of goal to date, projected 82% of goal, -3,204) and nearly out of untouched doors, so it is the clearest case for new doors [view:v_office_pace].
- Second passes only make sense later as a fallback on not-home doors [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass].

Method: capacity = last 7 days' average daily doors × 16 days left (Oct 19 to Nov 3) [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]; a second pass adds a door on the day of that pass [doc:counting-doors#doors].
